title: How a Squandered Democratic Trifecta Is Pushing Michigan Left
author: Drop Site News
content:
Polls close throughout most of Michigan at 8 p.m. ET tomorrow, and results in
the closely watched race between Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens will be
coming in quickly. In Missouri, Cori Bush is locked in a rematch with Rep.
Wesley Bell, who knocked her out of Congress with a then-record-setting amount
of money from AIPAC. In Michigan and also in Washington state and Virginia
there are a number of other critical races we'll be watching.

**On Tuesday morning at 9:30 am ET, we 'll be hosting our regular livestream
on YouTube and Twitter.** Then on **Tuesday evening at 7:30 pm ET we 'll go
live** with Krystal Ball at both the [Drop
Site](https://www.youtube.com/@DropSiteNews) and [Breaking
Points](https://www.youtube.com/@breakingpoints) YouTube pages, and we'll
track the results until we have a winner. We'll have a number of interesting
guests coming through, though I don't want to make any promises, because
election nights can be chaotic. Tune in if you can. Either way, we'll be
watching a historic night unfold.

_Story by Tom Perkins_

More than a dozen anti-establishment candidates running on populist economics
and Israel policy are threatening to take seats now held by Democrats across
Michigan, from U.S. Senate to city councils.

A sweep or strong showing by these insurgents in Tuesday's primary would be
seismic, upending Democratic Party power dynamics in an establishment
stronghold. More broadly, if the Democratic Tea Party comes for the bellwether
state of Michigan, the results would show that a new bottom-up politics is
taking root, providing the clearest signal yet that the fundamental shift in
the party underway is not restricted to New York or heavily blue cities.

(A full list of the races to watch on Tuesday, plus a handful already
concluded, is at the end of this story.)

To understand the moment here, one needs to look at the night of November 8,
2022, when midterm returns trickling in across Michigan slowly began to reveal
a surprise result: Democrats had won a trifecta and [gained control over the
state government](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/nov/17/michigan-
democrats-state-senate-house) for the first time in 40 years.

To many in the party, it felt like the state was emerging from the darkness
after decades of being unable to legislate under one of the nation's [most
gerrymandered maps](https://www.metrotimes.com/news/how-voters-were-screwed-
out-of-the-state-they-wanted-2380421/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), suffering under
GOP governors like Rick Snyder, architect of the Flint water crisis.

This kind of coverage matters. Make sure we can keep doing it:

Rank-and-file Democrats expected that wildly popular proposals they supported
would move easily into policy: making corporations pay for pollution, taxing
the wealthy, dramatically expanding healthcare, addressing the soaring cost-
of-living for the working class, and reining in DTE Energy, among the nation's
most expensive and unreliable utilities.

These proposals did not pass. Most of the economic agenda died. No one was
held responsible for Flint.

Pro-business Democrats in [leadership
positions](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2024/12/16/michigan-
house-democrats-frustration-with-speaker-joe-tate-boils-over-leadership-
detroit-mayor/77020311007/), including Gov. [Gretchen
Whitmer,](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/22122025/michigan-gov-gretchen-
whitmer-environmental-record/) [thwarted the most meaningful
proposals](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2024/12/16/michigan-
house-democrats-frustration-with-speaker-joe-tate-boils-over-leadership-
detroit-mayor/77020311007/) while cutting the [Covid safety
net](https://bridgemi.com/children-families/56000-michigan-kids-could-lose-
child-care-federal-covid-funding-ends/). The largely [squandered
trifecta](https://www.propublica.org/article/governor-gretchen-whitmer-legacy-
michigan-botched-legislative-session) and
[failure](https://www.bridgedetroit.com/dems-go-it-alone-in-michigan-house-
where-chaotic-meeting-ends-in-lame-duck-limbo/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) to
address Michigan's most urgent economic needs infuriated the base.

The party's failures to enact popular legislation dovetailed with outrage over
the establishment's [attacks](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2025/jun/06/michigan-university-gaza-surveillance) on [pro-Palestinian
advocates](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/michigan-democrats-student-
protesters-palestine-israel-elections) and [disrespect
of](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/06/michigan-senate-race-
democrats) Michigan's huge Arab-American populations; centrist Democratic
support for an onslaught of data center plans in the state; and the relentless
prioritization of corporate interests over residents' needs. The state's
powerful unions began inching away from corporate Democrats.

This confluence of forces ignited the groundswell of support for the 15
grassroots change candidates now on the ballot. Some have already won this
cycle, and the rest may make major gains on Tuesday.

**Yousef Rabhi** is a Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) member aiming to
unseat a 12-year party machine mayor in Ann Arbor, the state's most liberal
big city. He is up 13 points per [a late July
poll](https://www.dataforprogress.org/blog/2026/7/28/in-ann-arbors-democratic-
mayoral-primary-voters-back-challenger-yousef-rabhi-and-public-control-of-
their-electricity).

"Ultimately a lot of the major landmark legislation that they promised just
did not get delivered," he told Drop Site. "Now there's this combination of
rank-and-file working people, progressive activists and folks from all over
the political spectrum, people from Black, Arab, Jewish communities, who are
feeling overlooked by Democratic party right now, and there is surge surge of
left candidates where there is disaffection."

In the race for U.S. Senate, the latest polls put former Detroit health
department director **Abdul El-Sayed** up by 10-15 points over Rep. **Haley
Stevens** despite at least $30 million in spending by pro-Israel groups. The
Bernie Sanders-endorsed, former Sunrise co-founder **William Lawrence** is up
15-25 points in a mid-Michigan U.S. House seat, though establishment polling
has him behind. **Donovan McKinney** , backed by Justice Democrats and
Sanders, was running slightly behind the AIPAC-backed incumbent Shri Thanedar
in a poll on the Detroit U.S. House district race.

Downballot, former Uncommitted Movement co-founder and Sanders endorsee
**Abbas Alawieh** is attempting to be the first Arab-American to serve in the
state senate, and to represent Dearborn, a city with a huge Lebanese-American
population. Alawieh previously served as a congressional aide to Reps. **Andy
Levin** and **Rashida Tlaib** of Michigan, as well as **Cori Bush** -- who is
mounting her own comeback bid in St. Louis on Tuesday. In a Detroit state
house district, **Chris Gilmer-Hill** , backed by the DSA and Working Families
Party, is running against State Rep. **Helena Scott** , a pugnacious machine
politician.

But the insurgents face headwinds. The congressional races are awash in
corporate and pro-Israel lobby money. Pro-Israel donors [are
opposing](https://michiganadvance.com/2026/07/31/pro-israel-donors-fuel-
onwenu-in-contentious-detroit-area-state-senate-primary/) leftist Yemeni-
American state Senate candidate **Abe Aiyash** , and they account for about
one-third of the $353,000 raised by his opponent, the establishment-backed
**Justin Onwenu**.

Meanwhile, many older, [conservative black voters
here](https://www.metrotimes.com/news/why-isnt-detroit-the-nations-blackest-
big-city-ready-for-criminal-justice-reform-25497324/) have rejected Sanders-
style politics, and division exists among them and Arab-Americans. The left
has also been so weak in Michigan that there is little infrastructure like
that which the DSA and Working Families Party laid for many years in New York
that was essential to Zohran Mamdani's win, and the June "socialist sweep."

Still, the Working Families Party and DSA are [both gaining
strength](https://michiganadvance.com/2026/04/01/working-families-party-bets-
on-organizing-to-reshape-michigan-politics/) and active this cycle. And there
may be an "Abdul effect," said Bernie Porn, a state pollster with EPIC-MRA:
"El-Sayed's strength will probably translate into strength for all anti-
establishment candidates."

## **Gaza and Economic Frustration Dovetail**

The Democratic trifecta culminated with an acrimonious intra-party lame duck
fight at the end of 2024, as pro-business Democrat House Speaker **Joe Tate**
sat on popular bills, including nine that passed the legislature. Among them,
legislation to lower healthcare costs for unions, expand working class tax
credits, address predatory debt collectors, and fund an African-American
history museum.

Democrats had lost the house in the November election, and instead of sending
the bills to Whitmer for a signature before the trifecta ended, Tate handed
them to incoming GOP leadership, which also refused to send them to the
governor.

The state supreme court, controlled by Democrats, ruled several weeks ago that
the bills had to be sent to Whitmer for signatures. Instead, Whitmer quickly
vetoed them.

Labor viewed Whitmer's move as a "betrayal," a top official with one of the
state's largest unions, who declined to use their name to speak freely, told
Drop Site. Michigan is a labor stronghold, but 50 years of establishment
policies weakened it. Too many Democrats still try to "walk the line" between
corporate and labor interests, the union official said.

"When we took back the trifecta for the first time in 40 years, it was great
that the party in charge shifted, but the reality is that the largest
corporations in the state still were the ones who were setting the agenda at
the governing table," the union official added.

Increasingly, the union has a hardline position, the official added: "You
fight for workers or you do the bidding of corporations, but you cannot do
both as Democrats have tried, and there's a reckoning right now because of
that."

However, there is no labor effort to support "leftist" candidates, the
official said. Instead, they back candidates who unequivocally choose workers
over corporate interests. In Michigan, that more frequently means candidates
like El-Sayed, who also received a major endorsement from the American
Federation of Teachers that is part of the AFL-CIO, and even a Wayne County
Sheriff's Office union. Rabhi, a union member who has joined others on the
picket line, has support from the local teachers' union that has never
previously endorsed in a mayoral race, he said. Local chapters of AFSCME and
the UAW have also endorsed him, as have the AFT and National Nurses' Union,
among others.

This translates into material support on the ground. Earlier this year, in
Three Rivers--the type of small, west Michigan town where El-Sayed needs to do
well to win the nomination--he joined a UAW picket line. The union won an $8
per hour raise in a 10-day strike, and, in response, the union mobilized a
door knocking campaign for El-Sayed, who won over some Trump voters there.

The UAW also took a surprise step in voting to divest from Israel over its
genocide, which drew [retribution](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/uaw-shawn-
fain-neil-barofsky-recording-israel-gaza) from the Trump administration.
Meanwhile, economic discontent among Michigan's Arab-American and Muslim
communities added to frustration over establishment hostility to Arab-
Americans and pro-Palestinian advocates.

The establishment ignored the 100,000 "uncommitted votes" in Michigan's 2024
Democratic presidential primary, and steadfastly refused to change course on
its support for Israel's genocide. Though no data on how many uncommitted
voters did not vote for Kamala Harris in the general exists, she lost the
state by 80,000 votes, and election data showed [a loss of
about](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/nov/09/democrats-lose-
michigan-arab-american-voters) 22,000 votes in the three cities with the
highest Arab-American and Muslim populations alone.

It appears the establishment learned little. It launched attacks in late March
against El-Sayed for campaigning with **Hasan Piker** , broadly over their
criticisms of Israel. The media attacks, led by State Sen. **Mallory
McMorrow** , then El-Sayed's opponent, came as Israel was invading Lebanon,
and destroying cities in which many local Lebanese-Americans have roots,
family members, and friends. Some [community leaders
warned](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/06/michigan-senate-race-
democrats) that the Democratic establishment was ignoring their pain, and
making the same mistakes as 2024.

Weeks later, Gaza and economic discontent drove upsets at a contentious April
Democratic nominating convention, where leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney
**Amir Makled** beat the pro-Israel, establishment candidate **Jordan Acker**
for University of Michigan regent. Acker had led the U-M attack on pro-
Palestinian students. And **Eli Savit** , a progressive prosecutor, defeated
the [corporate, pro-Israel-backed](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/university-
of-michigan-regents-who) **Karen MacDonald** for the state attorney general.

Within months of the Piker controversy, McMorrow dropped out as she lagged in
the polls, and El-Sayed broke out as the front runner.

The economic frustration is not separate from dismay over establishment
support for Israel for Arab-American and Muslim voters here, and Gaza is many
issues wrapped into one, said **Bilal Baydoun** , a political analyst in
Dearborn.

"Supporting the genocide in Gaza is a statement on where Democratic priorities
are and it's an identifier where people say 'Look they're sending billions of
dollars to Israel, and I haven't heard of anything they're doing for my
kids,'" Baydoun said. "People say 'I was able to afford a home in my country--
I don't think my kid can do that anymore.'"

[A survey conducted in April, sponsored by Drop Site News and
Zeteo,](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/michigan-senate-democratic-primary-
poll-aipac) found that 62% of Michigan Democratic primary voters agreed that
they are less likely to trust a candidate would stand up for Michiganders in
general if they won't stand up to AIPAC; 13% disagreed with this sentiment.

## **Can Anti-Establishment Candidates Win in Detroit and Ann Arbor?**

In Ann Arbor, where Rabhi and a slate of four other candidates are attempting
to put a major dent in the corporate political machine that has ruled for 12
years, voters' concerns are a microcosm of the state and federal levels.

"People say that for 12 years the rent has gone up, the cost of living has
gone up, the roads have fallen apart, and city services have not been meeting
the needs of the residents," Rabhi said.

But Michigan is a diverse state and though the 15 candidates generally support
the same policies, campaigning on the east side of Ann Arbor may look
different than on the east of Detroit.

One recent poll shows El-Sayed behind in Detroit 66-33. Part of this may be
the conservative older population. And[ tensions
exist](https://michiganadvance.com/2026/05/29/taylor-alawieh-seek-to-unite-
black-and-arab-american-voters-in-michigan-senate-bids/) between [Black people
and Arab-Americans ](https://x.com/samueljrob/status/2080758781634310654)in
Detroit, which [in part stems from](https://www.metrotimes.com/food-drink/why-
are-there-no-black-owned-grocery-stores-in-detroit-3123958/) anger with gas
station, party store, and grocery store owners in the city who are largely
Chaldean and are accused of mistreating their mostly Black customers.

Some, like Eboni Taylor, a Sanders endorsee running for in a state Senate
district on Detroit's largely Black east side, actively avoid the "leftist"
label, and make clear they do not have an association with the DSA.

While campaigning, Taylor talks about maternal health, bringing down childcare
costs, and rejecting corporate money because "these are common sense things
that people want," Taylor said. "Working class families are waiting their turn
to be heard and for policy to work for them, and that's what is resonating for
them with my campaign."

When she navigates nursing homes or other areas where her list of progressive
endorsements does not carry a lot of currency, she connects with people by
talking about her history in the Baptist church, struggles raising kids, and
watching her working class parents who still live in the same east side home
build a better life for her.

However, Detroit City Council Member **Denzel McCampbell** , a former
spokesperson for Rep. Rashida Tlaib, openly campaigned and won this cycle as a
DSA member in a largely Black, low-income district on Detroit's west side, and
survived his opponents attacking him for being socialist.

"On the doors, what it meant to be a socialist did not come up - what came up
is 'You're not going to sell us out, right?'" McCampbell said. "That's what's
connecting--'Are you going to be an authentic leader that fights for us?'"

### **Key Michigan races:**

  * **Abdul El-Sayed** versus Rep. **Haley Stevens** for U.S. Senate.

  * **Bernie Sanders** -endorsed former Sunrise co-founder **William Lawrence** is running against two establishment candidates, **Matt Maasdam** and **Bridget Brink** in the 7th Congressional district.

  * Justice Democrats/Sanders-backed **Donovan McKinney** is running against the AIPAC-backed incumbent **Shri Thanedar** in the 3rd Congressional district.

  * DSA member U.S. Rep. **Rashida Tlaib** is running for re-election against the establishment-backed Inkster Mayor **Byron Nolen** in the 12th Congressional district.

  * Uncommitted co-founder and Sanders-endorsed **Abbas Alawieh** is running against state Rep. **Erin Byrnes** in Michigan state Senate district 2.

  * Leftist former state Rep. **Abe Aiyash** is running against establishment pick **Justin Onwenu** in Michigan state Senate district 1.

  * Sanders-endorsed **Eboni Taylor** is running against a long list of establishment-backed candidates in Michigan State Senate district 3, including Whitmer administration veteran **Korey Hall**.

  * DSA and WFP-backed **Chris Gilmer-Hill** is running against incumbent state Rep. **Helena Scott** in Michigan state House district 8.

  * Progressive prosecutor **Eli Savit** beat the establishment and pro-Israel-backed candidate, **Karen McDonald** , for state attorney general at the April Democratic nominating convention.

  * Leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney **Amir Makled** beat the establishment, pro-Israel-backed candidate, **Jordan Acker** , for U-M board of regents at the April Democratic nominating convention.

  * DSA member **Yousef Rabhi** is running for mayor of Ann Arbor with a slate of four other leftists candidates who are running for city council seats. **Chris Taylor** is the incumbent mayor.

  * DSA member and former Tlaib staffer **Denzel McCampbell** won a seat on the Detroit City Council in late 2025, defeating former state Rep. **Karen Whitsett**.

  * DSA State Rep. **Dylan Wegela** , WFP-backed State Rep. **Tonya Phillips** , and WFP-backed **Jason Morgan** are all defending seats in the Michigan House.
